questions.key_step: Leave-out pair by residue mod 3, then zero-lead casework
questions.justification: Two-stage counting: choose which digit pair is dropped by residue, then handle the leading-zero restriction; several cases where a slip changes the total, no options to check. Easier than 2025-P1-Q10 (L4/5) as cases are non-overlapping.

questions.key_step: Inclusion-exclusion for strings containing all three digits
questions.justification: Two short parts; the key step is a standard surjection count 3^n-3*2^n+3. Routine chain.

questions.key_step: Distribute five distinct primes into three groups, handling factor 1 and repeats
questions.justification: Needs set-partition style casework with the 'factor 1' and 'not a set' cases; familiar but easy to slip on.

questions.key_step: Legendre's formula
questions.justification: One standard formula applied once.

questions.key_step: x^2-y^2 never 2 mod 4; exponent distribution for xyz=N
questions.justification: Two parts, each a standard single idea (parity mod 4; stars-and-bars on prime exponents).

questions.key_step: Pattern casework on repeated letters
questions.justification: Five patterns of repeats must be listed completely and counted; omission is the main risk, no options.

questions.key_step: At-least condition via complement or cases
questions.justification: Standard committee selection with three parts; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Choose repeated digits, then arrange the multiset
questions.justification: Standard pattern count chained in three routine steps.

questions.key_step: G.P. of powers of 3 becomes A.P. of exponents; parity count
questions.justification: One idea (exponents form an A.P.) then a short count.

questions.key_step: 361-1 = 360 = (n-1)k, count divisors
questions.justification: Routine reduction then divisor counting.

questions.key_step: Multiset selections by number of distinct flavours
questions.justification: Four parts, standard stars-and-bars/casework.

questions.key_step: Fix middle digit y: (y-1)(y+1) choices
questions.justification: Routine casework summed over y.

questions.key_step: (x-1)^x minus the all-rest state
questions.justification: One multiplication-principle step.

questions.key_step: 64 x 49 / 2 for non-attacking pair
questions.justification: One familiar move.

questions.key_step: Choose which matches are wrong: C(5,k)2^k
questions.justification: One familiar binomial idea repeated over parts.

questions.key_step: Order within each subject is fixed by places, so 9!/(3!)^3
questions.justification: Statement is ambiguous; the key step is seeing that places fix order, then a multinomial.

questions.key_step: Symmetric matrix: diagonal ones odd; case on diagonal
questions.justification: Casework with symmetry; a few cases.

questions.key_step: 2^n minus two empty cases, divided by 2
questions.justification: One familiar counting move.

questions.key_step: Divide 16!/(4!)^4 by 4! for identical groups
questions.justification: Standard equal-groups formula, plus matching the option's odd-product form.

questions.key_step: P1..P4 label the groups; split remaining 12 as 3+3+3+3
questions.justification: Needs the labelling insight and then option matching.

questions.key_step: P6 best of its group => partners from P7..P16
questions.justification: Rank condition turned into a restricted choice, plus equal-group division and matching to k.

questions.key_step: m lines give m-1 gaps
questions.justification: Direct observation.

questions.key_step: Sum of squares 1..8
questions.justification: Direct sum.

questions.key_step: Sum (m-r)(n-r) with standard series
questions.justification: Routine algebraic summation.

questions.key_step: nCr x D6
questions.justification: One familiar formula.

questions.key_step: Both blocks deranged: D5 squared
questions.justification: Two linked ideas (block structure plus derangement).

questions.key_step: Integers forced away from natural places: 5! x 5!
questions.justification: Needs the insight that the derangement condition is automatic.

questions.key_step: Five independent counting parts (stars and bars, collinearity, derangement, digit product, pairing)
questions.justification: Five short parts of mixed topics; each routine but a slip in one breaks the match.
